glosses: Se placer ou s’établir à un endroit.

examples.text: Après leur numéro, les acrobates s’étaient installés au tabac où il avaient fixé rendez-vous au manager des girls.

Des plantes américaines ont fait le voyage à travers l’Atlantique, […], et sont venues s’installer sur la côte basque : une Graminée Stenotaphrum s’y est même développée fort abondamment et est un élément essentiel de la végétation des environs de Bayonne et de Biarritz.

Cette maison n’est pas la résidence secondaire de l’un d’entre nous : on nous l’a prêtée. Et nous nous y sommes installés avant l’annonce du confinement, qui nous a pris de court alors que nous randonnions.

glosses: einen Gegenstand senken/auf den Boden legen

examples.text: „Ist der Krahn an Bord geschwungen, so werden die Körbe auf das Kommando ‚Hier‘ niedergelassen, ausgeschüttet und durch große eiserne Trichter in die Kohlenbunker geschaufelt, wo die Heizer über sie herfallen.“ [Anmerkung: ‚Krahn‘ ist veraltete deutsche Rechtschreibung]

glosses: sich setzen (beispielsweise auf einen Stuhl, den Boden); die Knie auf den Boden beugen

examples.text: „Sie haben einen Baum unter dem es einfach nur gemütlich ist, aber können sich dort nicht bequem niederlassen? Dann bauen Sie doch einfach eine Baumbank!“

„Er mußte sich zwischen den beiden ältesten [Töchtern] niederlassen: sie schenkten ihm Wein ein, legten ihm die besten Bissen vor und meinten sie hätten keinen schönern Mann auf der Welt gesehen.“ [Anmerkung: ‚mußte‘ ist veraltete deutsche Rechtschreibung]
„Der Gotte kamen die andern Weiber nach, und eine nach der andern ließ sich nieder ins Gras, vorsichtig die schönen Kittel in Sicherheit bringend, […]“
„Ein Taubenschwarm, der bisher den Glockenturm umflogen hatte, ließ sich jetzt vor dem Hause nieder.“
„Gemeinsam kehrten Johnny, Lucy und Jules ins Wohnzimmer zurück und ließen sich um den großen Teetisch nieder.“

glosses: sich an einem Ort ansiedeln; an einem Ort ein Geschäft eröffnen

examples.text: „1849 kehrte er […] in seine Vaterstadt zurück und ließ sich als Musiklehrer nieder […]“
Ärzte können sich in Deutschland nicht einfach an einem Ort niederlassen.
In den ländlichen Regionen finden sich nicht genügend Ärzte, die sich mit einer Praxis niederlassen wollen.
Die Pilgrim fathers ließen sich zuerst an der amerikanischen Ostküste nieder.
Viele Wikinger ließen sich in den eroberten Gebieten nieder und lebten dort friedlich als Bauern oder Handwerker.

Während der großen Fluthen, in der ersten Hälfte des 17 . Jahrhunderts (1634) zogen viele Friesen von den Halligen nach Föhr, und ließen sich in Wyk und dem Dorfe Rieblum nieder, […] [Anmerkung: ‚Fluthen‘ ist veraltete deutsche Rechtschreibung]
„Ein Uhu-Paar hat sich in einem Storchenhorst im Elb-Havel-Winkel niedergelassen. Es zieht bereits Junge auf.“

glosses: To conclude or resolve (something):
To determine (something which was exposed to doubt or question); to resolve conclusively; to set or fix (a time, an order of succession, etc).

examples.text: His fears were settled
She hopes to settle and questions about the plans.
The question of the succession to a throne needs to be settled.
It is a Pamphlet, [...] It will ſettle the Wavering, confirm the Doubtful, inſtruct the Ignorant, inflame the Clamorous, though it never be once looked into.

glosses: To conclude or resolve (something):
To conclude, to cause (a dispute) to finish.

examples.text: to settle a quarrel

glosses: To conclude or resolve (something):
To conclude, to cause (a dispute) to finish.
In particular, to terminate (a lawsuit), usually out of court, by agreement of all parties.
To conclude or resolve (something):
To close, liquidate or balance (an account) by payment, sometimes of less than is owed or due.

examples.text: The coffee was only surface wet and looked worse than it actually was and as he returned to the Reception Desk to settle his account and give back his room key, he was met again by the young man who was still wearing his rucksack.

glosses: To conclude or resolve (something):
To pay (a bill).

examples.text: to settle a bill

glosses: To conclude or resolve (something):
To adjust differences or accounts; to come to an agreement on matters in dispute.

examples.text: He has settled with his creditors.

glosses: To conclude or resolve (something):
To conclude a lawsuit by agreement of the parties rather than a decision of a court.

examples.text: Of course, certainty is a value in all systems of conflict of laws—including those of the United States. Certainty for litigants decreases litigation and transaction costs and increases the chances that cases will settle.

glosses: To place or arrange in(to) a desired (especially: calm) state, or make final disposition of (something).

examples.text: to settle my affairs
to settle her estate

glosses: To place or arrange in(to) a desired (especially: calm) state, or make final disposition of (something).
To put into (proper) place; to make sit or lie properly.

examples.text: The curate settled his collar, coughed, and, making an effort, knocked.
She twisted out from under the claim of his palm to settle her feet on the floor.
Pausing only to settle his cloak and set his Regent's circlet on his hair, he strode to the rail and waited.

glosses: To place or arrange in(to) a desired (especially: calm) state, or make final disposition of (something).
To cause to no longer be in a disturbed, confused or stormy; to quiet; to calm (nerves, waters, a boisterous or rebellious child, etc).

examples.text: God settled then the huge whale-bearing lake, / And Tenedos we reach'd; [...]
[I]t drawing towards night, and they hoping that ſleep might ſettle his brains, with all haſt they got him to bed; [...]

glosses: To place or arrange in(to) a desired (especially: calm) state, or make final disposition of (something).
To silence, especially by force.
To place or arrange in(to) a desired (especially: calm) state, or make final disposition of (something).
To kill.

examples.text: I poured a charge of powder over the nipple so as not tu miss goin' off if possible. Click! went the match,—up jumped the flock, or tried tu. As they bunched up, Peggy blazed intu 'em, settlin’ how many I didn't know, …

glosses: To place or arrange in(to) a desired (especially: calm) state, or make final disposition of (something).
To bring or restore (ground, roads, etc) to a smooth, dry, or passable condition.

examples.text: clear weather settles the roads

glosses: To become calm, quiet, or orderly; to stop being agitated.

examples.text: The weather settled.

[T]il the fury of his Highneſſe ſettle / Come not before him.

glosses: To become calm, quiet, or orderly; to stop being agitated.
To become firm, dry, and hard, like the ground after the effects of rain or frost have disappeared.

examples.text: The roads settled late in the spring.

glosses: To establish or become established in a steady position:
To place in(to) a fixed or permanent condition or position or on(to) a permanent basis; to make firm, steady, or stable; to establish or fix.

examples.text: And he settled his countenance stedfastly [upon him], until he was ashamed.

glosses: To establish or become established in a steady position:
In particular, to establish in life; to fix in business, in a home, etc.

examples.text: Now thirteen Years of Age were ſwiftly run, / When the fond Father thought the time drew on / Of ſettling in the World his only Son.
But I will settle him in mine house and in my kingdom for ever.

glosses: To establish or become established in a steady position:
In particular, to establish in life; to fix in business, in a home, etc.
In particular, to establish in pastoral office; to ordain or install as pastor or rector of a church, society, or parish.

examples.text: to settle a minister

glosses: To establish or become established in a steady position:
To formally, legally secure (an annuity, property, title, etc) on (a person).
To establish or become established in a steady position:
To make a jointure for a spouse.

examples.text: He sighs with most success that settles well.

glosses: To establish or become established in a steady position:
To become married, or a householder.

examples.text: As People marry now, and ſettle; / Fierce Love abates his uſual Mettle: [...]

glosses: To establish or become established in a steady position:
To be established in a profession or in employment.

examples.text: He is settled in the profession of law at Rochester, New York.

glosses: To establish or become established in a steady position:
To become stationary or fixed; to come to rest.

examples.text: But then the Wind came about, and ſetled in the West for many dayes, ſo as we could make little or no way, and were ſometimes in purpoſe to turne backe.

glosses: To fix one's residence in a place; to establish a dwelling place, home, or colony. (Compare settle down.)

examples.text: the Saxons who settled in Britain

glosses: To fix one's residence in a place; to establish a dwelling place, home, or colony. (Compare settle down.)
To colonize (an area); to migrate to (a land, territory, site, etc).

examples.text: the French first settled Canada
the Puritans settled New England

It was in the year 1794, that an English family went out to settle in Canada.

glosses: To move (people) to (a land or territory), so as to colonize it; to cause (people) to take residence in (a place).

examples.text: Rome began to settle displaced or disenfranchised citizens, veterans, and allies in colonies beyond Italy.

glosses: To sink, or cause (something, or impurities within it) to sink down, especially so as to become clear or compact.
To clear or purify (a liquid) of dregs and impurities by causing them to sink.

examples.text: to settle coffee, or the grounds of coffee

glosses: To sink, or cause (something, or impurities within it) to sink down, especially so as to become clear or compact.
To cause to sink down or to be deposited (dregs, sediment, etc).

examples.text: to settle the sediment out of the water

glosses: To sink, or cause (something, or impurities within it) to sink down, especially so as to become clear or compact.

examples.text: to settle the chips in the potato chip bag by shaking it

glosses: To sink, or cause (something, or impurities within it) to sink down, especially so as to become clear or compact.
To sink to the bottom of a body of liquid, as dregs of a liquid, or the sediment of a reservoir.
To sink, or cause (something, or impurities within it) to sink down, especially so as to become clear or compact.
To sink gradually to a lower level; to subside, for example the foundation of a house, etc.

examples.text: Sometimes a tub will settle at one corner, causing the rim to slope.

glosses: To sink, or cause (something, or impurities within it) to sink down, especially so as to become clear or compact.
To become compact due to sinking.

examples.text: The chips in the bag of potato chips settled during shipping.

glosses: To sink, or cause (something, or impurities within it) to sink down, especially so as to become clear or compact.
